Creates a build session context, connects an MSBuild worker to it, runs the action against the connected context, and releases the worker afterward. Use for synchronous out-of-band evaluations (the MAUI deploy providers) that do not go through a full build request and so never get the request-completed teardown. The context never escapes this method, so callers do not manage the session lifetime themselves. If context creation fails, it returns default(T) without running the action.

member.summary: Synchronous counterpart of the command processor's async connect (OnMsBuildConnectionCompleted): waits on the connection task with a timeout, builds the session, and publishes it.
member.remarks: The wait blocks on purpose. runs only from the deploy providers, which DeploymentBackendHost starts on a dedicated background thread (lifetime.StartBackground) that has nothing to do until the worker is connected; it is not the executor or UI thread. The connection runs on its own background thread (MsBuildConnectionFactory.CreateAsync), so the wait cannot deadlock, and the timeout bounds it. An async deploy path would free this idle thread but would force both deploy providers async, which is not worth it here.
